notes.title: Client Update 5/2/2017
notes.content:
Redux's first month of beta went well, thank you to everybody who is participating.  The most common crash bugs were fixed and community feedback has shown which Redux features need be implemented next.

May's development will focus on finalizing the Steam Workshop addon support in Redux, this includes publishing new addons & full support for legacy addons.

A new Redux feature called Backpacks will be used to organize assets and prepare your addon before you share it to the Steam Workshop.

Backpacks & improved Steam Workshop support will be the 2 major features I'll be pursuing in April, but I will still be attempting to get as many smaller feature fixes & improvements in, as always.

[b]With that, here is the change log for today's client update 5/2/2017:[/b]
[list][*] Improved debug info for people affected by a crash when un-pausing AArcade.
[*] Added a Vimeo scraper.
[*] Updated the YouTube scraper to create items of type "videos", same as the Vimeo scraper does.
[*] Added WEBP image support to the image loader.
[*] Fixed the Steam Store scraper to work once again.
[*] Improved the YouTube player to support URLs that have a playlist in addition to a video ID.
[*] Renamed the Task Menu to the Tab Menu because it will have multiple tabs.  These tabs all have things that you will frequently want quick access to.
[*] Added a Commands tab to the tab menu with commonly used Source engine commands.
[*] Added a Tasks tab to the tab menu.
[*] Added a Screenshots tab to the tab menu.
[*] Improved the tab menu to remember which tab you last viewed in it.
[*] Added an Addons > Mounted Games menu that lists which Source engine games you have mounted.  This menu will be improved in future updates. [/list]

[h1][b]NOTE[/b][/h1]
Pushed a hotfix at 3:46pm Pacific time to fix the Create Shortcut menu to work with non-YouTube shortcuts again.

notes.title: AArcade: Redux Beta now live!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6721978/d9f27f0cd8d68ceefbd6656ccea8f24e6b7d9dfe.jpg[/img]

Hello again everybody!  It has been almost 1 year since I warned that I was going to go off the grid as I worked on a complete re-write of AArcade.  Almost 1 full year without updates to AArcade, and now, it's time for the first public version of the *all-new* Anarchy Arcade: Redux Beta!

Here are some known limitations & missing features in Redux Beta that you'll want to be aware of.  When all of these limitations are resolved, Redux will be very close to coming out of Early Access.

[h1]Beta Limitations[/h1]
[list][*] No multiplayer yet.
[*] Internal resolutions are not adjustable yet.
[*] No publishing content to the workshop yet.
[*] Can't launch other Source engine games yet.
[*] Can't "hard pause" yet. (Only has an improved "minimal" pause mode.)
[*] Open-with apps cannot be configured yet.
[*] Various missing features.
[*] No consumer-quality VR support yet.[/list]

[h1]Workshop Content[/h1]
All of your current workshop subscriptions from Legacy Mode will also continue to work in Redux.  Note that some [b]very[/b] old workshop items (referred to as "GEN 1") aren't supported yet.

[h1]Already an AArcade user?[/h1]
Now that Redux is public, all of your old AArcade stuff is in Legacy Mode.  You can launch Legacy Mode and use your old stuff like regular, OR you can EXPORT your legacy stuff so you can use it in Redux Mode as well.

notes.title: Dev Update: Redux & New Web Browser
notes.content:
The next update to AArcade is huge... a complete rewrite actually. The powerful Steamworks web browser is the first of the major changes that have been built into the new Redux version.

[h1][b]Brief History of AArcade[/b][/h1]
AArcade has been through a lot. Starting way back in 2010, AArcade's prototype saw its 1st public release onto ModDb and GameJolt.

Soon after it was greenlit for release onto Steam.

This was followed by a failed Kickstarter campaign attempting to raise funds for a full version.

After this major setback, I decided to continue working on the prototype independently to see the concept through to completion. This required lots of adjustments to AArcade's original design to make it an achievable project for a lone indie dev, such as myself, to complete.

A second, much smaller Kickstarter campaign was successful in raising nearly $2,000 which contracted artists to create game cabinets & other art assets for the project.

AArcade's souped-up prototype was released onto Steam as an Early Access title on 9/4/2014. Updates & improvements continued for the next year and a half.

In early 2016 it became apparent that Valve was focusing on other game engines, such as Source 2, and that Source 1 would sooner, rather than later, become outdated. Rather than let AArcade die from being tied to an outdated game engine, I decided to do something a little crazy. I started work on a complete re-write of AArcade, with the intention to future-proof the concept so we're never exclusively tied to any particular game engine. It would also give me the opportunity to fix or improve [b]many[/b] other issues of AArcade that existed due to lack of foresight on my part when designing the prototype all those years ago.

[h1][b]AArcade's Next Version: Redux[/b][/h1]
The next major update to AArcade is expected to be [b]available for public testing on Steam in early 2017[/b]. It is code-named AArcade: Redux and is actually a complete re-write of the old prototype from the ground up.

[b]The technical goals of the redux version are:[/b]
[list][*]Feature parody, including backwards compatibility, with [b]all[/b] previous versions of AArcade.[/*][*]Cross-engine compatibility, including abstraction of engine-specific assets, of library meta data.[/*][*]Clear distinction between meta library data and engine-specific AArcade frontends.[/*][*]Optimize performance, user experience, and modability of the Source engine frontend.[/*][/list]
While a majority of the dev work will be under-the-hood, it has already begun to manifest itself in some very long-awaited improvements & feature enhancements that users have been requesting over the years.

There's so much good new stuff in the redux version that I couldn't possibly show you all the development progress in a single post. So I'll start with showing you just one of the awesome new behind-the-scenes enhancements to AArcade and what it means to you, as a user.

[h1][b]Steamworks Web Browser[/b][/h1]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AFpydb8IskU
One major change is to the old embedded web browser which has been completely replaced by the state-of-the-art Steamworks browser. In fact, it is the same browser that Steam itself uses! Compatible with Netflix, Twitch, and so much more, users can make full use of their favorite web content on the in-game screens.

Speaking of the in-game screens, AArcade: Redux has a new multi-threaded embedded instance framework which allows things like web tabs, emulators, or media players to playback on the in-game screens with minimal performance impact.

And speaking of performance impact, how about running 2, 3, or 4 web tabs at the same time? AArcade: Redux makes this possible, and distributes the task of web tab rendering over multiple frames to keep your in-game performance consistent.

[h1][b]AnarchyArcade.com's Massive Update[/b][/h1]
Last month Anarchy Arcade's website received a massive update with [b]tons[/b] of info about AArcade's concept, its focus, and where its headed in the future. I'd appreciate it if you went and checked out my work there! There's even some stuff on there, like the 360 panoramas, that I will be explaining/showcasing in future dev updates: http://www.anarchyarcade.com/

[h1][b]Thanks for your support![/b][/h1]
I want to thank everybody who's contributed to AArcade and showed their support over the years. Thanks to all the Kickstarter backers. Thanks to everybody who's donated through PayPal. Thanks to everybody who's Tweeted about AArcade or shared it with their friends. And thanks to all the users who help each other out in the forums or put that extra effort in on their workshop submissions.

Even though I use AArcade a whole lot myself, it's great to be able to share it with others, and it's support from people like you all that makes that possible. Party on!

notes.title: Multiplayer Building & Shared Online Saves
notes.content:
Last week Metaverse Mode was introduced as an alpha feature.  This is a very significant feature and will change the course of AArcade development as it heads towards coming out of Early Access on Steam.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dFMx2K14MFI

[h1][b]Metaverse Mode Features[/b][/h1]
[list][*] Online persistent arcade save that [b]EVERYBODY[/b] shares for [b]EVERY[/b] map.
[*] Every map is a multiplayer server when it's loaded in Metaverse Mode.
[*] Live multiplayer building & item editing.
[*] VERY fast map & arcade loading (even faster than singleplayer!)
[*] Optimized cabinet spawning (stuff doesn't spawn until you get near it!)
[*] Easy to use (just click Metaverse Mode, no more port forwarding!)
[*] Griefer-resistant database (all of a banned user's changes can be reverted!)
[*] Compatible with 99% of singleplayer features.[/list]

[h1][b]Metaverse Mode Limitations[/b][/h1]
[list][*] Only 1 player avatar (soon to be fixed.)
[*] No auto-downloading of workshop content (soon to be fixed.)
[*] No way to host your own singleplayer saves in metaverse mode (soon to be fixed.)
[*] No syncing of which video/object people are watching (soon to be fixed.)
[*] No voice chat.
[*] No peer-to-peer file transfers of custom models & textures.
[*] In-map entities such as doors & elevators are not synced.[/list]

I expect those top 4 limitations to be fixed within a month.

[h1][b]FAQ[/b][/h1]
[list][*] Q: Can other people see the stuff I spawn?
A: Yes.  Everything you spawn or change is synced.
[*] Q: Am I uploading my stuff?
A: No.  You are only sharing image URLs for textures and meta information about the shortcuts such as its title & description.
[*] Q: Can other people move or delete the objects I spawn?
A: Yes.
[*] Q: What if I use workshop addon content?
A: Workshop content works fine, but people who are not also subscribed to the content will see small tablets as placeholders for the models they are missing.
[*] Q: Is everybody else forced to watch what ever I click on?
A: No. However, soon there will be a way to allow this type of behavior for groups of players who want to stay synced up to each other.
[/list]

Until the bugs are all worked out, metaverse mode is not as stable as singleplayer yet and it will likely crash more often.  Do you have long launch times in AArcade? Then I [b]recommend[/b] using Launch w/ Preview Mode when opening AArcade.  It uses an alternate aarcade folder with no workshop content and no game mounts so you can get right into the metaverse.

[h1][b]How To Use Metaverse Mode[/b][/h1]
[list][*] Go to Main Menu > Options > Arcade Options and Enable Online Play.
[*] Notice the players-per-map count that is now shown on the Main Menu.
[*] Go to Main Menu > Play > Play Custom and choose any map.
[*] Click the green Metaverse Mode button to load the map in Metaverse Mode.[/list]

On a very exciting related note, this new optimized way that the Metaverse Mode spawns objects means we could now potentially have many thousands of objects on a single map without excessive lag because only objects we get close to get loaded in. :)

[h1][b]Coming Next Month...[/b][/h1]
[list][*] Custom metaverse player avatars
[*] Metaverse Steam workshop support
[*] Metaverse player groups & group viewing
[*] Host your own singleplayer arcades in "Personal Metaverse" mode![/list]

Here is one of my arcades that you'll be able to come check out in the metaverse next month once we are able to host our SP arcade saves:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l-zrxa5BzMY

notes.title: Client Update 1/26/2016
notes.content:

notes.title: Client Update 1/20/2016
notes.content:
[list][*] Fixed the "Toggle Physics" button (o). Press it to turn an object into physics. Use the Physics Pick Up button (v) to pick things up & put them down.  Don't forget to re-freeze them to save their spawn position.
[*] Removed malfunctioning gameplay timers from items.
[*] Removed obsolete tutorial video progress from the HUD.
[*] Added the ability to enable/disable the following HUD elements from the Arcade Options menu: High Scores, Controls, Item Details, Item Title, Arcade Details, Crosshair.
[*] Fixed the glow around selected objects. Enable/disable it from the Arcade Options menu.
[*] Added "Fast(er) Workshop Loading" to the Arcade Options menu.  When enabled, it will load workshop items without taking the time to display status messages.  This is faster, but the AArcade window will appear as if it is frozen while it loads workshop items.
[*] Added an alpha of a feature called Online Mode. It lets you see & eventually interact with other players even while using AArcade as your singleplayer desktop.
[*] Added an Online Mode options to the Options > Arcade Options menu.  (Leave "Show Own Phantom" OFF! Or you won't see other people's zombies like you should.)
[*] Added a player count per-map of Online Mode players to the Main Menu.[/list]

[b]NOTE:[/b]
VR mode is still broken until the Source SDK Base is updated to the newest engine branch.

[h1][b]Online Mode (ALPHA FEATURE)[/b][/h1]
To bridge the gap between the many members of the AArcade community, today's update introduces a new feature called Online Mode. If you want to try it out, go to the Main Menu > Options > Arcade Options and turn on Online Mode.

Online Mode will sync the name of the map you are in to a web server.  It will also sync your current position and rotation to the web server.

This means that you'll be able to see other people walking around your maps, even in singleplayer mode!

Soon more interaction will be possible, but right now you'll just see other players in the map as zombie torsos. :)

There is a list of maps on the Main Menu now along with the player count in each of them. Using maps with more players is a higher chance of running into some zombie people.

The live online session is powered by Firebase and can also be viewed in Chrome at: http://www.anarcast.tv/spectate.html

Better spectating features will come in the future as well.

[h1][b]Advanced Users[/b][/h1]
If you've already configured AArcade to use advanced features such as Libretro sound, you will once again need to re-copy the libretro-enabled client.dll into your bin folder after this update.

This might be a very handy command to use as well:
obtain_cab trading_card; obtain_cab trading_card_big; obtain_cab trading_card_big_table; obtain_cab trading_card_table;

notes.title: Anarchy Weekly Issue No. 6 - To-Do List
notes.content:
Engine update, public to-do list, preparing for release, my epic new VR PC build, and more Twitch fun.  Lots of news to bring you arcade maniacs today, so let's get started!

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue6/awheader.png[/img]
[b]Last week AArcade was updated to Valve's 2015 build of the Source engine,[/b] giving us lots of fixes and improvements.  This update was a major step towards AArcade coming out of early access, which is planned to happen within the next couple months.

The 2015 engine build allows AArcade to load maps from the TF2 workshop that used special compression methods, giving us even more compatible addon maps to play around in.  Shadows have been improved and can now stretch to match the light source position.  Valve also included many VR and security updates in the latest engine build, along with other improvements and fixes that I haven't even discovered yet.

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b][url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/source-sdk-2013/commits/master]Valve Software GitHub[/url][/b][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue6/todolist.jpg[/img]
[b]With the help of the AArcade community, I have compiled a public to-do list of nearly 200 fixes & features that we want added to AArcade.[/b]  While only a handful of these are expected to be added before the full Steam release, the list will be used to guide continued development after release as well.

The sortable list can be found by going to [url=http://anarchyarcade.com/?page_id=206]http://www.anarchyarcade.com[/url] and clicking on "To-Do List" in the navigation bar.  If you feel that the list is missing a bug fix or a feature that needs to be added, feel free to voice your opinion in a reply to this news article or on the forums.  And keep an eye on the list as it may change over time as people submit new ideas or as items on the list get completed.

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b][url=http://www.anarchyarcade.com/?page_id=206]Anarchy Arcade Website[/url][/b][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue6/preprelease.png[/img]
[b]AArcade has way more features than it lacks,[/b] so a big part of coming out of Early Access is documentation, tutorials, and videos that show people what AArcade is capable of, and how to use it. This includes a rennovation to AnarchyArcade.com, the Steam store page, and in-game help menus.

AArcade can be used for LOTS of different things, so quickly showing a new user exactly what they want to know about it can be a challenege.  I've decided that the best way to address this is to have a set of [b]short, very specific videos[/b] on the website that allow users to jump directly to the topics that interest them.  The first two videos that I created for the series are below:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q37m008b8z8
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7EISw3jKFxc
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kOLTwdXktxM

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b][url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCi0WsH_8LBxqS3ZfYoydiIQ] Anarchy Arcade YouTube[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=http://www.anarchyarcade.com/?page_id=206]Anarchy Arcade Website[/url][/b][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue6/preprelease.jpg[/img]
To help with development and testing, last week I built a BEAST of a VR gaming PC. It far surpasses the recommended VR specs released by Oculus & Valve. With it I will be able to properly test VR support & multiplayer servers in AArcade, as well as take the Wednesday Twitch streams to a whole new level!  Did I mention that Source engine games & AArcade have their own dedicated 500GB SSD? I have included links to the parts I used in case anybody is thinking about building their own rig.

[b]Specifications:[/b]
[list][*]Intel i7 6700k
[*]NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980TI AMP!
[*]16MB DDR4 RAM[/list]

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b][url=https://www.oculus.com/en-us/oculus-ready-pcs/]Oculus Recommended Specs[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=http://www.amazon.com/dp/B012M8LXQW/]My CPU[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=http://www.amazon.com/dp/B00YNEIAWY/]My GPU (AMP! model)[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=http://www.newegg.com/Product/Product.aspx?Item=N82E16813132567]My Mother Board[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=http://www.newegg.com/Product/Product.aspx?Item=N82E16811352020]My Case[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=http://www.newegg.com/Product/Product.aspx?Item=N82E16820231878]My RAM[/url][/b][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue6/videogameawesome.png[/img]
If you like games, or if you like AArcade, or if you just have a 2nd monitor with nothing playing on it, be sure to tune into the LIVE weekly video stream from my garage where I use my totally tricked-out one-and-only IRL Anarchy Arcade cabinet to build arcades and play games in literally all day long.

Thanks to the new PC, AnarchyTV now has some excellent stream quality broadcasted at low bitrate so even people with slow internet can drop in and hang out with me.

Last Wednesday I logged some SERIOUS playtime in the following games during the stream:
[list][*]Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege (Max Settings)
[*]Star Wars Battlefront (Max Settings + Logitech Flight Stick)
[*]Grand Theft Auto V (Max Settings + G27 Racing Wheel + 360 Controller)[/list]

I'll be playing games from AArcade all day on Wednesday, but as always I will be able to answer any questions or demonstrate anything you need in AArcade.

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b][url=http://www.twitch.tv/AnarchyArcade]Anarchy Arcade Twitch Channel[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IrePSVBU3G0]Power Glove Guy's YouTube Video[/url][/b][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue6/nextweek.png[/img]
In other community news, there have been some awesome workshop shares the past few weeks as well as some excellent nodes shared using the new & improved metaverse node system.  In next week's article, I will be focusing on these and other AArcade community events as usual.

http://store.steampowered.com/app/266430/

notes.content:

[*] Added the ability to enable/disable workshop items without unsubscribing from them.
[*] Changed the Manage Addons menu to reflect the new workshop enable/disable system.
[*] Fixed an issue that caused node objects to be non-colidable the first time they were spawned.
[*] Fixed an issue that caused node objects to take a very long time to spawn.
[*] Added the boolean console command "keepscore 0".  When set to 1, the score of your arcade will not be calculated, which makes things faster on very large arcades.
[*] Added a default fade distance for all objects.
[*] Added the console variable "fade_dist" to control the default distance at which objects fade.
[*] Added a shorter fade distance for node objects.
[*] Fixed an issue that would cause 2 instances of nodes to be spawned ontop of each other.
[*] Fixed various timeouts and "loopback" issues in very large arcades.[/list]

[b]Note 1:[/b] Remember there is a SKIP TUTORIAL button on the very bottom right corner of the screen if you get prompted to do it again.

[b]Note 2:[/b] If you have large screens in your arcade that are too far away to be visible with the new prop fading system, you can adjust the fade distance with the console variable: fade_dist.  Soon this option will be added to the in-game Arcade Options menu as well.

[b]Note 3:[/b] This update is the precursor for the Halloween update that will put user-generated content in the spotlight with the improved "Metaverse Node" features and meta maps.  Expect another update within a couple weeks that polishes up all of the new features that you see here.

notes.title: Anarchy Weekly No. 5 - Metaverse
notes.content:
[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue5/awheader.png[/img]

[b]Take the red pill[/b], then imagine everything that exists, then add to that everything that is fictional.  That is what the metaverse [b]is[/b].  This vast sea of information [b]has always been there[/b], but navigating it has never been this fun.

In this issue we explore just how deep the rabbit hole goes by taking a close look at [b]just one room[/b] of a community-made arcade share.  In the process, we reflect on what the metaverse itself is and what it means to traverse it as a gamer.

[url=http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue5/theater.jpg][img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue5/thumbnail.jpg[/img][/url]

[h1][b]The metaverse is [u]real[/u].  It's not a game.[/b][/h1]

Let's put things in perspective.  The screenshot above shows what it's like to BE an arcade cabinet in Anarchy Arcade.

However, what you *see* in this still picture is only scratching the surface.  In this particular room exists the blood, sweat, and tears of hundreds of fellow human beings all to provide you with thousands of hours of joy & entertainment.

Welcome to the metaverse.  [b]Every single cabinet acts as a portal that whisks you away into a whole new universe.[/b]

You'll [b][u]look[/u][/b] different.  You'll [b][u]move[/u][/b] different.  You might even [b][u]feel[/u][/b] different.  That's because each universe is its own reality.  Each one is uniquely tailored to provide you with a particular experience.

Some universes let you bring your Steam friends along.  Others only let you bring your friends who are physically with you.  And yet others can only be explored with the loneliest number.  [b]What ever the realities may be, you are subject to them when you enter their universe.[/b]

So when you see this screenshot, it's not just a room full of arcade cabinets.  It's a massive [b]slice of the metaverse that is being visualized by Anarchy Arcade.[/b]  And even though this slice is so massive, it's still only a tiny sliver of what exists.

[h1][b]References (seen in screenshot):[/b][/h1]
[list][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hitman:_Codename_47]Hitman: Codename 47[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_Slug_3]Metal Slug 3[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euro_Truck_Simulator_2]Euro Truck Simulator 2[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APB:_All_Points_Bulletin]APB: Reloaded[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac-Man]Pac-Man[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Fortress_2]Team Fortress 2[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Mario_Kart]Super Mario Kart[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_Race_64]Wave Race 64[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keen_Software_House#Medieval_Engineers]Medieval Engineers[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dota_2]Dota 2[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_City_Ransom]River City Ransom[/url][*][url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donkey_Kong]Donkey Kong[/url][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue5/javascript.png[/img]
[h1][b]JavaScript & HTML5 Modding in AArcade[/b][/h1]
[b]Anarchy Arcade uses JavaScript to create 3D representations of 2D web pages.[/b]  The scripts that do this are called "scrapers".  Until now, users were only able to use the scrapers that I programmed.  These let you spawn things from sites like Twitch, YouTube, Netflix, Hulu, etc.  

As of last week's update, users are able to start AArcade with the new +enable_user_scripts 1 launch option and use their own custom JavaScripts on their own favorite sites.  Instructions & tutorials are not yet available for modding the UI or writing your own scrapers, so you'll be on your own for now.  The files that will interest you are in the aarcade/protectedscripts folder.  Note that you [b][u]must[/u][/b] launch with the [b]+enable_user_scripts 1[/b] launch option for your customized scripts to be loaded.  The launch option is required for security purposes.

[h1][b]Refrences:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/266430/announcements/detail/52143616512476437]Client Update 8/25/2015[/url][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue5/sharkweek.png[/img]
Last week Discovery launched the website www.discoveryvr.com.  It features some awesome 360 videos that are great for viewing from inside of Anarchy Arcade.

[h1][b]Watch this video for an explanation and demonstration:[/b][/h1]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sGxPAGHyxxo

[h1][b]Refrences:[/b][/h1]
[list][*]http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=507875440[*][url=http://www.discoveryvr.com/]DiscoveryVR[/url][/list]

notes.title: Anarchy Weekly No. 4 - Sequels
notes.content:
[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue4/awheader.png[/img]
In this trip around the metaverse we combine the [b]original Star Wars trilogy[/b] with the [b]all-new The Force Awakens universe[/b], AArcade-style. We also take a look at [b]Source 2[/b], the sequel to the Source engine, and where it fits into AArcade's plans for the future!

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue4/awimagehr.png[/img]
When you think about being stranded in the desert, an arcade is probably not the 1st thing that comes to mind. But to an experienced AArcade user, even the barren planes of [b]Tatooine[/b] can feel like home.

When you have a nice, cool Sandcrawler to take shelter in, the heat of the desert isn't so threatening. You can even go for a [b]hover-in[/b] movie right in the middle of the day! In the screenshot I'm watching scenes from Star Wars: The Force Awakens on a giant screen that I placed on the side of the Sandcrawler, turning it into a rolling drive-in movie theater!

In addition to the arcade built inside of the Sandcrawler itself, there is also a nice, cool Krayt dragon cave to take refuge in, a moisture farmer's homestead, and a crashed transport ship to get you out of the hot desert sun. I've heard rumors of a Sarlacc in the area, but have never found it. Be cautious! And may the Force be with you! This awesome GMod community map was created by the very talented Lord Trilobite!

[b]Note:[/b] You need to have Counter-Strike: Source mounted to use this map in Anarchy Arcade.

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b]Rp_Tatooine_Dunesea (the GMod map shown in the screenshot)[/b]
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=216974337[*][b][url=http://steamcommunity.com/id/lordtrilobite/myworkshopfiles/]Map Author's Steam Workshop (Lord Trilobite)[/url][/b][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue4/awimagehr2.png[/img]
If you've been keeping up with state-of-the-art game engines, you've probably heard of Unreal 4, Unity 5, or even CRYENGINE as they all compete for the attention of next-gen developers. What you may not have heard about is Valve's own next-gen engine called Source 2, which has been brewing for its glorious public release for years.

[b]First of all[/b], you can already see a young version of Source 2 in action in Valve's game Dota 2 Reborn.

[b]Second[/b], the map editor for Source 2, called Hammer, is a newer version of the Source 1 map editor, also called Hammer.

[b]Third[/b], based on interviews, Valve seems to be building Source 2 specifically around UGC and mountable content, even more so than Source 1, which already has unparalleled cross-game content sharing & UGC features. User generated content, or UGC, consists of the game's community and everything that the community creates & shares with each other.

[b]Fourth[/b], Valve has partnered with HTC to create the premium home virtual reality hardware/software experience that will be available to gamers some time before 2016. What in-house engine does Valve use to develop & test this state-of-the-art technology? You guessed it! Source 2. Seems like a no-brainer that Source 2 is where you'll want to be for VR development.

And in case you haven't heard about VR, it ain't no joke! It's like you're standing INSIDE of your favorite environments. The Vive even lets you stand up and walk around! Watch out for the pooch! Still not convinced? Well, check out this 360 degree screenshot and multiply its coolness by infinity. It's a math thing.

[url=http://www.anarchyarcade.com/vrscreen/?id=outset2][h1][b]Click here to view 360 degree screenshot of Anarchy Arcade[/b][/h1][/url]

So where does Source 2 fit into future of Anarchy Arcade? Honestly, we can't be sure until I get my hands on it to see what its backwards-compatibility is like. Then we, as in the AArcade community and myself, can determine if a Source 2 Anarchy Arcade is something that could be an update, or would need to be a sequel itself.

Either way, [b]the future of the Anarchy Arcade we know and love it today is as solid as ever![/b] With hundreds of thousands of addons and unparalleled cross-game content sharing, the Source 1 engine is a great place to be! We can only hope that Source 2 is able to stand on the shoulders of all this great existing content and be truly epic on day 1!

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]

[*][b][url=https://www.unity3d.com/]Unity 5[/url][/b]

notes.title: Anarchy Weekly No. 4 - Sequels
notes.content:
[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue4/awheader.png[/img]
In this trip around the metaverse we combine the [b]original Star Wars trilogy[/b] with the [b]all-new The Force Awakens universe[/b], AArcade-style. We also take a look at [b]Source 2[/b], the sequel to the Source engine, and where it fits into AArcade's plans for the future!

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue4/awimagehr.png[/img]
When you think about being stranded in the desert, an arcade is probably not the 1st thing that comes to mind. But to an experienced AArcade user, even the barren planes of [b]Tatooine[/b] can feel like home.

When you have a nice, cool Sandcrawler to take shelter in, the heat of the desert isn't so threatening. You can even go for a [b]hover-in[/b] movie right in the middle of the day! In the screenshot I'm watching scenes from Star Wars: The Force Awakens on a giant screen that I placed on the side of the Sandcrawler, turning it into a rolling drive-in movie theater!

In addition to the arcade built inside of the Sandcrawler itself, there is also a nice, cool Krayt dragon cave to take refuge in, a moisture farmer's homestead, and a crashed transport ship to get you out of the hot desert sun. I've heard rumors of a Sarlacc in the area, but have never found it. Be cautious! And may the Force be with you! This awesome GMod community map was created by the very talented Lord Trilobite!

[b]Note:[/b] You need to have Counter-Strike: Source mounted to use this map in Anarchy Arcade.

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b]Rp_Tatooine_Dunesea (the GMod map shown in the screenshot)[/b]
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=216974337[*][b][url=http://steamcommunity.com/id/lordtrilobite/myworkshopfiles/]Map Author's Steam Workshop (Lord Trilobite)[/url][/b][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue4/awimagehr2.png[/img]
If you've been keeping up with state-of-the-art game engines, you've probably heard of Unreal 4, Unity 5, or even CRYENGINE as they all compete for the attention of next-gen developers. What you may not have heard about is Valve's own next-gen engine called Source 2, which has been brewing for its glorious public release for years.

[b]First of all[/b], you can already see a young version of Source 2 in action in Valve's game Dota 2 Reborn.

[b]Second[/b], the map editor for Source 2, called Hammer, is a newer version of the Source 1 map editor, also called Hammer.

[b]Third[/b], based on interviews, Valve seems to be building Source 2 specifically around UGC and mountable content, even more so than Source 1, which already has unparalleled cross-game content sharing & UGC features. User generated content, or UGC, consists of the game's community and everything that the community creates & shares with each other.

[b]Fourth[/b], Valve has partnered with HTC to create the premium home virtual reality hardware/software experience that will be available to gamers some time before 2016. What in-house engine does Valve use to develop & test this state-of-the-art technology? You guessed it! Source 2. Seems like a no-brainer that Source 2 is where you'll want to be for VR development.

And in case you haven't heard about VR, it ain't no joke! It's like you're standing INSIDE of your favorite environments. The Vive even lets you stand up and walk around! Watch out for the pooch! Still not convinced? Well, check out this 360 degree screenshot and multiply its coolness by infinity. It's a math thing.

[url=http://www.anarchyarcade.com/vrscreen/?id=outset2][h1][b]Click here to view 360 degree screenshot of Anarchy Arcade[/b][/h1][/url]

So where does Source 2 fit into future of Anarchy Arcade? Honestly, we can't be sure until I get my hands on it to see what its backwards-compatibility is like. Then we, as in the AArcade community and myself, can determine if a Source 2 Anarchy Arcade is something that could be an update, or would need to be a sequel itself.

Either way, [b]the future of the Anarchy Arcade we know and love it today is as solid as ever![/b] With hundreds of thousands of addons and unparalleled cross-game content sharing, the Source 1 engine is a great place to be! We can only hope that Source 2 is able to stand on the shoulders of all this great existing content and be truly epic on day 1!

notes.title: Anarchy Weekly No. 3 - Strength in Numbers
notes.content:
[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue3/awheader.png[/img]
Each week [b]*cough*[/b] this newsletter highlights awesome content from around the Anarchy Arcade community. But who [b]IS[/b] this community? How many people actually play? This issue will fill you in on some of the [b]exciting[/b] stats about the community.

In addition, there are some [b]new community-made cabinets on the workshop[/b] this week that you're sure to get a kick out of. Let's get to it!

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue3/numbers.png[/img]
There are a lot of different places to get stats from: [url=http://steamcharts.com/app/266430]SteamChats[/url], [url=http://steamspy.com/app/266430]SteamSpy[/url], and the developer stats. While they all vary slightly, most calculations seem to agree with each other. So here's the run-down of what AArcade's community & player base is like:

[h1]Players in the last 2 weeks:[/h1]
[b]16 thousand[/b]

[h1]Peek concurrent players per-day:[/h1]
[b]80[/b]

[h1]Steam Workshop shares:[/h1]
[b]1,337 (I'm serious)[/b]

[h1]YouTube videos watched from inside AArcade last month:[/h1]
[b]175 thousand[/b]

[h1]YouTube videos watched from inside AArcade this year:[/h1]
[b]1 million 77 thousand[/b]

And the year isn't over yet! It's great to see a community forming around AArcade that not only gets enjoyment from using it, but also makes it a better place to be by helping each other out on the forums and sharing onto the Steam workshop. You all deserve an applause!

It's very inspiring to see so many people getting the kind of enjoyment out of Anarchy Arcade that I had in mind when creating it. I've noticed everybody's patients as I fix/improve things one at a time working towards a quality good enough to remove that Early Access label and it is duly appreciated. [b]Thanks for playing![/b]

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b][url=http://steamcharts.com/app/266430]SteamCharts profile for Anarchy Arcade[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=http://steamspy.com/app/266430]SteamSpy profile for Anarchy Arcade[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/266430]Steam Community for Anarchy Arcade[/url][/b][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue3/awimagehr.png[/img]
Even though the name Invict hasn't been mentioned in Anarchy Weekly before, he is pretty well known among the community either personally or through [b]his awesome workshop shares.[/b] Well, last week Invict decided to step it up a notch by learning to take regular 3D models from sites like tf3dm.com and turn them into [b]game-ready dynamic arcade models[/b] that can be used in Anarchy Arcade.

His new workshop share includes the [b]awesome stand-up flight cabinet shown in the screenshot[/b] that adds some much needed variation to your flying arcades. You also get some other great all-new (to us, anyways) cabinet models ported over by [b]Invict[/b]. Invict would also like to thank OkeDoke for teaching him the basics of Blender and how to create Anarchy Arcade models in general! Nice teamwork guys!

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b]Cabinet Pack by Invict[/b]
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=498090607[*][b][url=http://tf3dm.com/3d-model/space-harrier-upright-arcade-machine-81406.html]daystar65's Space Harrier Upright Arcade Machine 3D model[/url][/b][/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue3/atvheader.png[/img]
AnarchyTV's live all-day [b]Wednesday[/b] stream has been going strong [b]weekly from 6am - 10pm.[/b] Most recently we had another Twitch streamer, xDraLLoCx, win the Steam gift giveaway and receive Fallout: New Vegas! So congrats to him and to the previous week's winner who received Zombie Driver HD! I hope you guys are enjoying your games and drop by the stream again in the future for more [b]fun & giveaways![/b]

It's also a great place to come see what Anarchy Arcade is like to use as your 3D desktop and ask about any questions or concerns you have. And most of all, have some fun! Until next time [b]be excellent to each other and party on, dudes![/b]

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b][url=http://www.twitch.tv/AnarchyArcade]AnarchyTV Twitch Channel[/url][/b][/list]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/266430/

notes.title: Anarchy Weekly No. 2 - Toontastic!
notes.content:
[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue2/awheaderno2.png[/img]

What could be more exciting than issue no. 1 of Anarchy Weekly, [b]YOUR peek into the metaverse that exists all around us?[/b] That's right, issue [b]no. 2![/b]

This week we'll be stepping inside of our favorite cartoon... and never come out. Because we don't have to! Anarchy Arcade enables us turn [b]any[/b] Source engine map into our [b]working desktops![/b]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue2/awimagehr2.png[/img]
Fans of the show [b]Courage the Cowardly Dog[/b] will already recognize the kitchen that Fry is standing in up there. That's right, [b][url=http://steamcommunity.com/id/Modestyiswimpy]modestyiswimpy[/url]'s[/b] awesome fan-made GMod map makes the perfect desktop for your PC!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p1pJjfrQc5s

Similarly to GMod, [b]AArcade is able to mount the assets from over 30 other Source engine games![/b] That means all of the official & community addon maps, models, and other assets from these games can be enjoyed seamlessly as [b]your personal 3D desktops.[/b]

Just go to the Main Menu > Options > Manage Addons to get started with mounting games in Anarchy Arcade.

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b]Map Author's Steam Workshop (Modestyiswhimpy)[/b]
http://steamcommunity.com/id/Modestyiswimpy/myworkshopfiles/

[*][b]gm_middle_of_nowhere (the GMod map shown in the screenshot)[/b]
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=110979635[*][b]Chart of Mountable Content for Anarchy Arcade[/b]
http://imgur.com/59HmLlb[/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue2/atvheader.png[/img]
[h1][b]Using AArcade to Play Games & Movies LIVE[/b][/h1]
[b]Every Wednesday I broadcast LIVE from 6am - 10pm PDT[/b] on [b][url=http://www.twitch.tv/AnarchyArcade]twitch.tv/AnarchyArcade[/url][/b]. If you don't believe that AArcade can deliver on its amazing features & want to see them in action for yourself, or if you just want to see what an experienced player's 3D desktops can look like, [b]stop in any time during Wednesday and say hello![/b]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue2/giveawayheaderno2.png[/img]
Every week I give away a gift copy of one of my Steam game to a viewer. Last week it was WWE 2K15 and a very dedicated WWE fan spent all day idling the stream waiting for his chance to win. Fate would have it that when the 3 top-scoring vieweres names were put on the prize wheel and it was given a big spin, it landed right on him. So congrats to last week's WWE 2K15 recipient [b]WWETHEJAWZZ[/b] for trying so hard and having it pay off in the end!

[b]This week I have an extra copy of Zombie Driver HD[/b] with YOUR name on it! Anybody can win, and [b]you don't even need to have Anarchy Arcade to participate![/b] Just drop into the live Twitch stream any time during [b]Wednesday between 6am - 4pm PDT[/b] and interact with the chat bot to get on the viewer score board. The 3 top viewers with the most points will be added to the prize wheel at 4pm PDT to determine the [b]1 lucky viewer that will receive the Steam game. Have fun![/b]

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b][url=http://www.twitch.tv/AnarchyArcade]AnarchyTV Twitch Channel[/url][/b]
[*][b][url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/220820/]Zombie Driver HD on Steam[/url][/b][/list]

notes.title: Anarchy Weeky First Issue! Featuring 360 YouTube Video Spheres
notes.content:
[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue1/assets/awheader.png[/img]
[b]Welcome to the first issue of Anarchy Weekly![/b] Its mission: [b]to bring you the latest & greatest news, addons, and highlights coming from the Anarchy Arcade community and from all corners of the world![/b]

I'm [b]SM Sith Lord[/b] and I'll be your host & curator for this wild ride through [b]the metaverse of all human knowledge, history, fiction, and future.[/b]

Our first issue focuses on an awesome submission by an AArcade community member, so without further adieu, lets get started!

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue1/assets/awimagehr.png[/img]

[h1][b]YouTube 360° Video Spheres[/b][/h1]
Recently YouTube added 360-degree streaming videos to their service. These videos allow you to look around in any direction as if you were actually there in real life!

Fortunately for us, AArcade community member [b][url=http://steamcommunity.com/id/oke_doke]Oke Doke[/url][/b] was able to make a 360° video sphere cabinet for us to spawn these new videos in! Fry has a bunch of them spawned in this parking lot here (above). [b]You just stand in the middle of the spheres and enjoy the show with a fully interactive 360° viewing experience.[/b]

Oh, and did I mention that [b]last week Valve fixed Steam's VR mode[/b] so you can now experience the 360° videos inside of your arcades with Facebook's [b]Oculus Rift[/b] or [b]HTC's Vive virtual reality[/b] devkits!

[h1][b]References:[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b]360° Video Sphere & Panoramic AArcade Addon Cabinets[/b]
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=442750783[*][b][url=https://www.youtube.com/results?filters=spherical&lclk=spherical&search_query=video]360° YouTube Videos[/url][/b]

[*][b][url=http://css.gamebanana.com/maps/139716]mcdonalds-mds-v2-beta (the CSS map shown in screenshot)[/url][/b]

[*][b]Philip J. Fry (the GMod player model shown in the screenshot)[/b]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=279330893[/list]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue1/assets/atvheader.png[/img]
[h1][b]AnarchyTV Live Twitch Demonstrations[/b][/h1]
The all-new AnarchyTV interactive Twitch.tv video stream will be [b]LIVE all-day this Wednesday, July 29th between 6am - 10pm PDT![/b] Come see what it's like for somebody to launch games from Anarchy Arcade as I try to make progress in beating various games from my library.

You can interact with the AnarchyTV live video stream through chat commands, and you even earn [b]AnarchyTV points[/b] for doing so! [b]The top 3 viewers with the most points at the end of the day get entered into a drawing to win a prize![/b]

[img]http://www.anarchyarcade.com/weekly/issue1/assets/giveawayheader.png[/img]
[h1][b]AnarchyTV Game Giveaway[/b][/h1]
If Twitch.tv is good for anything, its for giving away free stuff. This [b]Wednesday[/b] I will be gifting my extra copy of WWE 2K15 on Steam to the winner of the AnarchyTV raffle!

All you have to do is join the Twitch stream some time during Wednesday and interact with the chat bot for a chance to win your spot on the prize wheel. [b](You don't even need to have Anarchy Arcade!)[/b]

[b]The wheel will spin at 4pm PDT with the top 3 names on it. The winner gets WWE 2K15 and is invited to be my tag-team partner in multiplayer mode! :D[/b]

notes.title: Client Update 7/5/2015
notes.content:
[list][*] Improved Steam game videos take up more of the cabinet screen space.
[*] Added "Custom Shortcuts" to the filters of the File Open Browse dialog. This allows a desktop shortcut to have custom launch options added to its target field, which is required to launch games like SMITE.
[*] Improved startup times.
[*] Improved the speed and responsiveness of the embeded web browser.
[*] Fixed an issue that prevented players from setting certain console commands in AArcade's launch options.
[*] Improved the stability of all multi-threaded features such as: image downloading & Windows browse/save dialogs.
[*] Added a "Save As" dialog to the embedded web browser.
[*] Added the ability to download files to your PC from the embedded web browser (you always get the "Save As" prompt first.)
[*] Added CoolText to the Internet menu.
[*] Added automatic spawning of downloaded logos from CoolText.com.
[*] Added a "Please try again" message for when downloading a logo from CoolText.com fails.
[*] Added "Load Batch Size" to the Arcade Options menu. It controls how many items get loaded before a loading progress update is shown.  Cranking it up to MAX will disable progress updates all together, for the fastest possible load times, but will cause the AArcade window to appear unresponsive sometimes.
[*] Added the launch option +workshop to AArcade to enable/disable Steam workshop features (for debugging).  By default, workshop is always enabled.  To disable it, use +workshop 0 in your launch options.  Only do this if you are trying to troubleshoot very long startup times.
[*] Fixed an issue that would cause games with apostrophes in their title to fail at finding artwork on the TheGamesDb.net.
[*] Fixed the Oculus Share spawner to work with VR experiences that have no preview video.[/list]

notes.title: Client Update 7/3/2015
notes.content:
[list][*] Fixed the Steam workshop timestamps on the Manage Addons menu.
[*] Improved startup time.
[*] Changed the Custom Game menu to better accomdate a large number of maps.
[*] Fixed the dates shown for workshop items on the Addons menu.
[*] Added a BACK button on various menus.
[*] Added a Map Info menu that shows detailed information when you click a map on the Custom Game menu.
[*] Added a screenshot cycler to the Map Info menu that lets you cycle through all of your screenshots on that map.
[*] Added an instance picker to the Map Info menu that lets you pick which save instance you want to load.
[*] Added a Media Preview to the Map Info menu that shows you detailed information about every shortcut in an arcade before you load it.
[*] Added a Host Server sub-menu to the Map Info menu.
[*] Added the ability to specify workshop content that will automatically be downloaded when joining your server.
[*] Added the ability to specify a game that is required to be mounted to join your server.
[*] Added the ability to specify if clients can directly download the map from you.
[*] Added an informative loading screen when mounting workshop content.
[*] Changed the over-the-head icons to now appear in singleplayer while in 3rd person camera view.
[*] Added marquee & video icons above your head for current selected and/or continuous play items (singleplayer only for now).
[*] Added alternative versions to the Anarchy Arcade/aarcade/bin folder with experimental features.
[*] Fixed an issue that caused AArcade's process to take a long time to fully close.[/list]

[h1]Libretro Sound Instructions[/h1]
This build of AArcade includes an alternative version of client.dll that you can swap out to enable sound of in-game videos and emulators.  If you wish to try out this feature:
[list][*] Close Anarchy Arcade.[*] Overwrite the following DLL file with the one from the "libretro_sound_enabled" sub-folder: [i]Anarchy Arcade/aarcade/bin/client.dll[/i]

Be sure to go into Arcade Options and set your libretro sound options afterwards.  The in-game emulator cores can be found on www.libretro.com.  Libretro is updated daily, but if you are new to Libretro, here is a good pack of cores to put into your [i]Anarchy Arcade/aarcade/cores[/i] folder: http://buildbot.libretro.com/nightly/win-x86/2015-03-25_cores.7z

As long as your regular Windows versions of the emulators are configured in Anarchy Arcade, the libretro ones will automatically work in-game.  Note that only 2D emulators have in-game support at this time.

notes.title: Client Update 4/9/2015
notes.content:
[list][*] Added a Skip Tutorial button to the Basic Training prompts.
[*] Fixed the reflections in the tutorial map.
[*] Changed F1 to bring up a selection of help videos to watch.
[*] Removed the old unlock system.
[*] Added a NEW unlock system that is managed by Steam stats.
[*] Added a fictional in-game currency called "tickets".  You earn tickets as you play, then you get to choose which unlocks to spend them on.
[*] Added an Achievements menu.  Use it to spend your tickets or check your stats.
[*] Added an Achievements button to the Message of the Day.
[*] Added an Addons menu.  Use it to manage your workshop subscriptions, game mounts, search providers, and emulator profiles.
[*] Added an Addons button to the Message of the Day.
[*] Fixed an issue with the basic training map that would reject certain valid image URLs.
[*] Added the console command "fixwebviews" to test a fix for an issue that could cause irresponsive web views.[/list]

[b]Unlock System Notes:[/b]
The new unlock is powered by Steam stats, so this is the very last time you will have to deal with re-unlocking your cabinets.  You normally earn tickets by doing things like launching games or decorating your arcades.  You will also earn large amounts of tickets for earning achievements.  There is a cheat code you can use that gives you 3,000 tickets if you are a veteran AArcade player and don't want to deal with unlocking your cabinets again.

To spend your tickets, you go to the Achievements menu to choose which prizes you want to unlock. All maps are UNLOCKED from the start, so they aren't even listed in the prize shop.  All cabinets & props are LOCKED from the start.  Just click the UNLOCK button next to the ones you want.

[b]Big $$$ Cheat Code[/b]
For a limited time only, you can use the following console command to give yourself 3,000 tickets instantly: vipstatus

Note that you can only use this cheat code once, and your stats will remember that you used it.  So only cheat if you are a veteran AArcade player and not interested in the new unlock system at all.

notes.title: Client Update 3/18/2015
notes.content:
[list][*] Moderately reduced the initial start up time of Anarchy Arcade for people who are subscribed to many workshop addons.
[*] Slightly reduced the loading times of all maps and arcade saves (in most cases).
[*] Optimized AArcade's cloud storage to further reduce initial start up / shut down times.
[*] Reduced the amount of disk space that AArcade uses for people who have many published workshop items.
[*] Added the console variable "libretro_time_per_frame" so users can control the number of milliseconds each frame should be displayed by the in-game libretro core.
[*] Fixed an issue that prevented users from publishing new items to the workshop if they already had many published items.
[*] Improved SteamVR & Oculus Rift support.
[*] If Steam is running in VR mode, websites you launch from AArcade will be displayed in the SteamVR Chromium browser instead.
[*] AArcade will now automatically be in VR mode if launched from Steam's VR mode.
[*] VR apps can now be launched from AArcade while it is in VR mode itself.

[h1][b]Oculus Rift Developer Notes:[/b][/h1]
If you are a developer wanting to test your Oculus Rift development kit with AArcade, these instructions apply to you!
I have personally used AArcade on the DK1, and others have used it on the DK2. You must have the newest Oculus Rift runtime utility running.  Your Rift must be in Extended Mode as your secondary monitor.  You must have DK1 Legacy App Support turned OFF, even if you are using a DK1.
Launching AArcade from Steam's VR mode will automatically start AArcade in VR mode.  Otherwise, you have to go into video options and enable VR.

notes.title: Client Update 3/8/2015
notes.content:
Today's update makes it easier than ever to share your arcade saves to the workshop, it also adds some neat features that users have been requesting.

[list][*] Allowed the libretro cores to run at framerates higher than AArcade.
[*] Added mouse-over cursors to the in-game web browser and UI.
[*] Changed the number of rewards shown per-page on the Collect Rewards menu to 20.
[*] Added a link to a list of which games can be mounted to the Mount Content menu.
[*] Changed the Packing Manager to automatically save changes you make to the form.
[*] Removed the Update buttons from the Packing Manager because they are not needed anymore.
[*] Increased the screenshot delay for the Packing Manager to fix broken thumbnail images.
[*] Added a Package Dependencies section to the Packing Manager that shows you what workshop & game mount dependencies it has.
[*] Changed the Packing Manager to show a much simplier menu when the package is empty.
[*] Added a "Learn More" button to the Packing Manager that explains how to use & publish to the workshop.
[*] Removed the ability for full arcade saves on hub_walls and hub_floors to be shared to the workshop. (They can still be used for sharing nodes.)
[*] Fixed an issue that caused custom workshop cabinets to be unusable. (Thanks to Orangestar for the solution.)
[*] Fixed an issue that sometimes caused workshop packages to have incorrect dependencies.
[*] Added the console variable "show_workshop_content_in_library", which is 1 by default.  When set to 0, workshop content will be NOT be listed in your Library Browser unless you are filtering specifically for workshop content.
[*] Changed the Publish button on the middle-click menu to open the Packing Manager like normal, since most new users were discovering the Packing Manager this way anyways.  Advanced users can still hold down SHIFT + click on the Publish button to add an individual cabinet or object to the package like before.
[*] Fixed an issue that would cause nodes to be broken when saved.[/list]

[b]Note:[/b]
Even though producting broken nodes has been fixed, I still need to add in code that fixes already-broken nodes.  So if you were having issues with nodes you saved, give me a couple more days to squash the last bugs!  Thanks for your patients!

notes.title: Workshop Re-Enabled & Wall Nodes Sharable!
notes.content:
[img]http://smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/workshopreenabled.png[/img]
AArcade's all-new and improved workshop update is now live!  Many Early Access users have already shared some amazing creations onto the workshop.

If you're new to using the Steam Workshop, AArcade makes it easy with a built-in packing & publishing tool!  You can share individual items, or entire arcades.

To share an arcade, just load up your arcade and press the P button to open the Packing Manager.  Click Pack Arcade Save and then fill out the rest of the details on the form.  After that, click Publish and be patient as your workshop item uploads.  As soon as it's finished, AArcade will open the workshop profile of your newly shared item in the Steam overlay.

Also new in this update is the ability to share & subscribe to nodes!  Just pull the lever next to a customized wall in the map named hub_walls to save your node and share it to the workshop!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GG822zJ-g8U

[h1]Technical Improvements[/h1]
[list][*] Uses the newest version of the Steamworks API.
[*] UNLIMITED workshop file size.
[*] UNLIMITED workshop shares.
[*] You don't need to subscribe to your own shares anymore.
[*] You don't need to store an extra copy of workshop items anymore.
[*] Backwards compatible with existing "legacy" workshop content.
[*] As always, shortcuts to local files have their folder paths hidden.[/list]

Remember that Anarchy Arcade shares media items themselves, not your copy of them.  That means that it's perfectly fine to share arcades that have shortcuts to games or movies on your PC.  Other people using your arcade would need access to their own copies of the games or movies to launch the shortcuts, and everybody can watch the preview videos regardless.

[img]http://smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/igg2014.png[/img]
Last year Anarchy Arcade participated in the Indie Games For Good charity pledge drive & marathon Twitch.tv stream ([url]http://www.iggmarathon.com/games/[/url]).  Hundreds of indie games participated, and in total the event raised over $19,000.00 US for the Child’s Play charity.  Pledgers were allowed to choose a game that they were most interseted in seeing played during the stream, and in the end AArcade was the 6th most requested game!

[img]http://smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/steamuniverse.jpg[/img]
Earlier this week Valve announced that they will be introducing SteamVR hardware and a refined Steam controller at the Game Developer's Conference in San Fransisco (March 4th - 6th, 2015).  This is exciting news for Anarchy Arcade users because AArcade uses the same VR integration as Team Fortress 2 itself which is devloped in-house at Valve.  For more information on SteamVR, check out their announcement: [url]http://store.steampowered.com/universe/[/url]

notes.title: January Updates (Part II)
notes.content:
[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/mapdiscovery.png[/img]
[h1]Map Discovery Awards[/h1]
AArcade supports over 50,000 maps.  Often you will load up what you believe to be the most epic map ever used in AArcade.  You also might believe that you are the first person in the world to ever use this awesome map as a 3d desktop.  Well now, thanks to the Steam leaderboards & AArcade's all new map discovery system, you can confirm this belief!

If you are the first person ever to load up a map in AArcade, your Steam name & avatar are for ever bound to that map in AArcade as the map's discoverer!  You will be listed on the TOP of the leaderboard for the map with a special note saying that YOU discovered the map first, as well as the number of players who discovered it after you.

The landrush is on!  Try to leave your mark on your favorite maps by being the first person ever to load them up in AArcade!  However, you might find that you aren't the only one who loves that map. :)

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/leaderboards.png[/img]
[h1]Steam Leaderboards[/h1]
In addition to remembering who discovered the map, the new leaderboards also record how much time each player has spent in the map (in total), how many times they have re-visited the map, as well as how many shortcuts they spawned in their arcade there.

As players, the leaderboards give you a good idea of what other players think of the map.  They also help you find friends that might be interested in doing some multiplayer in that obscure addon map that only you and 3 other people have discovered so far. :)

As map authors, it shows you how many people have loaded your map and how much time they spend on it.  Two stats that I would have LOVED to have back when I was publishing Counter-Strike: Source maps to CAL.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/extendeddev.jpg[/img]
[h1]Development Extended to End of February[/h1]
AArcade was supposed to be ready to come out of Early Access at the end of January; however, I saw the opportunity to add some awesome unplanned features (such as the ones covered in this article) and must extend the Early Access period to the end of February as I polish up the new features and get them release-ready.

I'd like to thank everybody who took part in December's successful Kickstarter campaign which funded AArcade all the way through January and made all of these great new features possible.  As the stretch goals promised, Black_Stormy was brought on board for the month of January and produced some great new cabinet models for us as well as created the first major Hub map which will be released in February's big update.  His awesome map will be the "Kickstarter Arcade" map that appreciatively displays the 2 logos of the Kickstarter patrons who pledged over $100 and brings the conclusion of the Kickstarter promises.  I hope that everybody is happy with the results.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/ppalback.jpg[/img]
[h1]PayPal Donations Are Back[/h1]
If you missed the Kickstarter or would like to continue to support Anarchy Arcade's development, PayPal donations have opened back up for anybody who wishes to contribute.  Note that the Kickstarter pledge rewards do not apply to PayPal donations.  The Kickstarter is over.

https://www.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr?cmd=_s-xclick&hosted_button_id=WDS7JAWZ4LJBS

If you are an Early Access user that wishes to donate, I suggest using the in-game Donation Rewards button instead as it will grant you a couple special in-game models for using it.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/partyon.jpg[/img]
[h1]Until Next Time[/h1]
Don't forget that you can personally ask me questions LIVE on my Twitch stream, every Wednesday from 4am - 10pm Pacific time at twitch.tv/AnarchyArcade.  I'll be happy to demonstrate how to do things in AArcade, answer any technical questions you might have, or just play vs you in some games.  Have fun in your 3D desktops and party on dudes!

In addition to remembering who discovered the map, the new leaderboards also record how much time each player has spent in the map (in total), how many times they have re-visited the map, as well as how many shortcuts they spawned in their arcade there.

As players, the leaderboards give you a good idea of what other players think of the map.  They also help you find friends that might be interested in doing some multiplayer in that obscure addon map that only you and 3 other people have discovered so far. :)

As map authors, it shows you how many people have loaded your map and how much time they spend on it.  Two stats that I would have LOVED to have back when I was publishing Counter-Strike: Source maps to CAL.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/extendeddev.jpg[/img]
[h1]Development Extended to End of February[/h1]
AArcade was supposed to be ready to come out of Early Access at the end of January; however, I saw the opportunity to add some awesome unplanned features (such as the ones covered in this article) and must extend the Early Access period to the end of February as I polish up the new features and get them release-ready.

I'd like to thank everybody who took part in December's successful Kickstarter campaign which funded AArcade all the way through January and made all of these great new features possible.  As the stretch goals promised, Black_Stormy was brought on board for the month of January and produced some great new cabinet models for us as well as created the first major Hub map which will be released in February's big update.  His awesome map will be the "Kickstarter Arcade" map that appreciatively displays the 2 logos of the Kickstarter patrons who pledged over $100 and brings the conclusion of the Kickstarter promises.  I hope that everybody is happy with the results.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/ppalback.jpg[/img]
[h1]PayPal Donations Are Back[/h1]
If you missed the Kickstarter or would like to continue to support Anarchy Arcade's development, PayPal donations have opened back up for anybody who wishes to contribute.  Note that the Kickstarter pledge rewards do not apply to PayPal donations.  The Kickstarter is over.

https://www.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr?cmd=_s-xclick&hosted_button_id=WDS7JAWZ4LJBS

If you are an Early Access user that wishes to donate, I suggest using the in-game Donation Rewards button instead as it will grant you a couple special in-game models for using it.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/partyon.jpg[/img]
[h1]Until Next Time[/h1]
Don't forget that you can personally ask me questions LIVE on my Twitch stream, every Wednesday from 4am - 10pm Pacific time at twitch.tv/AnarchyArcade.  I'll be happy to demonstrate how to do things in AArcade, answer any technical questions you might have, or just play vs you in some games.  Have fun in your 3D desktops and party on dudes!

notes.title: January Updates (Part I)
notes.content:
Lots of great new features such as watching 2 videos at once, real video projectors, and more! This article will briefly overview what's been added to AArcade during January development.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7U8K61tjxak

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/interactionaward.png[/img]
[h1]ModDb 2014 Editor's Choice[/h1]
AArcade was selected as one of ModDb.com's Editor's Choice for Mod of the Year 2014.  It's an honor to be recognized by ModDb and receive the "Interaction Award" for AArcade's use of the Source engine.  Be sure to check out the other great games on the list, such as Double Action Boogaloo, which took 1st place as the Editor's Choice Mod of the Year.
http://www.moddb.com/events/2014-mod-of-the-year-awards/features/mod-of-the-year-2014-editors-choice

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/twovideos.jpg[/img]
[h1]Watch Two Videos at the Same Time[/h1]
Do you like to party?  Do you think watching just one video at a time is like a baby's toy?  AArdade now lets you watch up to 2 different videos at the same time on how ever many virtual screens you want.  Just look at a video and hold down the R button to put it on continuous play.  You'll then be able to walk around and watch other videos without interrupting the one that's on continuous play.

That's not enough?  You want to see your video playing in every room of your house?  No problem.  Just use AArcade's existing "Video Slave" setting to have your video play on as many screens as you want.  How about... 100?  That'd look pretty cool.

Turn ANY screen into a slave screen by walking up to it, pulling out its Green Menu > Cabinet tab > Filters button and setting it to slave screen.  The screen will now mirror any video you have playing, like virtual AirPlay.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/cabanimations.png[/img]
[h1]Cabinet Animations[/h1]
AArcade now has an extensive cabinet animation system built right into each model.  This allows for awesome things like a TV that slides up from the ground when you turn it on, or a poster that unfolds into a video screen.  You'll also be able to give the joy sticks, wheels, and switches a good once-over as they bring the cabinet to life with animation.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/realprojectors.png[/img]
[h1]Dynamic Lighting, Spotlights, & Real Projectors[/h1]
Tired of turning on your flashlight to see your awesome arcades built in dark addon maps?  Well now, when you activate a cabinet, an animated dynamic light will illuminate the cabinet you selected as well as all of the props next to it.

Do you think that only 1 dynamic light at a time is like a baby's toy?  Well, now in AArcade you can spawn as many standalone spotlights & [b]real[/b] projectors as you want!

Projectors will show any video that you have playing, much like a slave screen.  These are [b]real[/b] projectors that will cast light on what ever you point them at.  And remember that [b]EVERY[/b] screen in AArcade is interactive, even light cast from a projector!  That means you'll be able to fulfill your dream of playing retro games projected onto a giant brick wall in the seedy alleyway of a city!

Behind the scenes, the dynamic lights work hand-in-hand with the new cabinet animation system to allow cabinets to spawn all sorts of entities and attach them to animated bones.  The projectors and spotlights are just the tip of the iceberg.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/autocam.jpg[/img]
[h1]Auto Camera Mode[/h1]
Showcasing your favorite media to yourself & to your friends has never been easier than now with auto camera mode!  Just walk up to any cabinet that supports it and press E to activate auto camera mode.  A custom animation sequence will play on the game cabinet as the camera automatically inspects the cabinet model, the artwork on it, and the video playing in it in a very cinematic style mini-cutscene.

From auto camera mode you can either launch & play your shortcut, or press ESC to go back to walking around.

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/hubsandnodes.jpg[/img]
[h1]Hubs & Nodes - a Taste of February Updates[/h1]
There is a big update coming in February that will allow you and your friends to work together in building the greatest VR arcades imaginable, even if you never play multiplayer!  It's called the HUB game mode and it's going to be the heart and soul of AArcade once it goes live near the end of February.

There are 3 major components to the HUB game mode: nodes, HUB maps, and the Steam workshop.  As of January, the first part of the puzzle, nodes, went live for Early Access users to try out and leave feedback.

[h1]Groups of Shortcuts (nodes)[/h1]
A node is a group of shortcuts that somebody created that can be easily spawned into your arcades as a cluster of objects all attached to each other.  The awesome thing about nodes is that no matter how many instances exist in how ever many maps, if you ever go and update your node by adding new songs to it or something, those changes also take effect in every arcade that uses that node.

As of January, Early Access users can now create their own nodes for use in their own arcades.  Even locally, nodes are a very exciting feature that let you quickly get your favorite songs and games into any arcade.  It's much faster than spawning your shortcuts one at a time, especially if you find yourself putting some of the same music & games into every map you visit.

In February's update, you will be able to share your own nodes to the Steam workshop, as well as spawn your friends' nodes in your own arcades.  When combined with the Steam workshop, nodes become even more awesome.  Thanks to nodes, you and your friends can now affect each other's worlds not only in multiplayer, but even while in singleplayer as well!  Workshop nodes are updated automatically when needed, so your friends will always see the most recent changes you've made to your node, right there in their own arcades!

[h1]Where Nodes Come Together (Hubs)[/h1]
Hubs are special maps that will be introduced in February's update designed specifically for community customization with workshop nodes.  Sort of like a mall, where the server operator (or the player in the case of singleplayer) decides which of their friends gets to "decorate" each store.  The end result of Hubs will be awesome community arcades, jam packed with the stuff that you and your friends care about the most, that are different every time you load it up.

Early Access users can start getting familiar with how nodes and hubs work right now because the January update featured 2 experimental Hub maps.  Only local nodes can be saved/used right now, but the February update will bring the Steam workshop connectivity into the mix!

[img]http://www.smarcade.net/dlcv2/moddb/steamstats.jpg[/img]
[h1]Steam Stats / Achievements[/h1]
In January, AArcade saw the addition of Steam Stats and received its first set of Steam Achievements.  This first set was focused mainly on the player's map-based stats & achievements.  Additional stats & achievements are planned to be added regularly.

[Continued in Part II of the announcement.]

notes.title: Client Update 1/31/2015
notes.content:
[list][*] Fixed an issue that gave you extra points for moving a cabinet.
[*] Changed the point value algorithm to divide the value of an item by the number of duplicates that exist in the arcade.
[*] Added a High Scores leaderboard for each map.  It keeps various stats like score & time played, but does not record any information about your personal shortcuts.
[*] Added the map discovery system.  Be the first person to load up a map in AArcade to be immortalized.
[*] Added the first set of Steam Stats & Achievements.
[*] Modified the map hub_walls to allow you to save cabinets spawned a couple feet from the wall.
[*] Added the map hub_floors.  It's just like hub_walls, but with floors.
[*] Fixed an issue that caused weird stuff to happen if you pressed E on a selected cabinet.
[/list]

[b]Map Discovery System[/b]
With this update, the brand-new Map Discovery system is live!  Be the first person ever to load up a particular map in AArcade, and you will be added to the leaderboard as the discoverer of that map!  The landrush is on!

[b]Delayed Release[/b]
I've been implementing so many new & unexpected features the past month that I must extend AArcade's development while I finish testing and polishing the new features.  Development is extended until the end of February.  PayPal donations will open back up soon if you wish to continue contributing.  Thank you to everybody who has contributed thus far.  I've been so busy coding and making art that I haven't had a lot of time to write news articles to keep you all informed of development.  Keep an eye out for a news article highlighting January's development soon!

notes.title: Client Update 1/28/2015
notes.content:
[list][*] Going to a fullscreen mode will automatically put the active video into your pocket (as long as there isn't something already playing in your pocket).
[*] Fixed an issue to allow physics props to be picked up with V button again.
[*] Fixed an issue to allow the map editor to compile working maps again.
[*] Added the ability to spawn multiple objects at once, called "nodes".
[*] Added the ability to create & save nodes (only local for now).
[*] Added a HUBs manager to the UI, activated by switches in hub_ maps.
[*] Added the addon map hub_walls.[/list]

[b]Note:[/b] This update shows the foundation of what the HUB gamemode is all about. Nodes are like groups of objects.  They can be anything from a simple wall, a room of a hotel, or an entire house of a neighborhood.  The map included with this update, hub_walls, is a simple wall for you to decorate.  You can only save your nodes locally right now, but soon the Steam workshop will be re-enabled and you will be able to share the nodes you have already made.

I created the map included in this update with a very specific purpose in mind, but I'm sure you'll find some creative uses for it.  I often find myself building music walls in my arcades with generally the same music.  By using the map hub_walls to create new "node" items, I will be able to spawn my music wall into new maps with a single click.  And if I ever go into hub_walls and update my music wall, it automatically gets updated in every map I've spawned it in.

Nodes are a new type of object that you can find in your Library Browser.  You can spawn them in any map, but HUB maps are specifically designed for them.  Nodes are groups of shortcuts.  When you spawn a node, it spawns a single tablet where you are looking with many other shortcuts attached to it.  If you delete that center tablet, all of the child shortcuts that belong to it get deleted too.  If you move a child shortcut out of a node, it breaks it from the node and becomes part of the larger arcade save.  Nodes do not automatically save.  You must flip the big leaver next to them to save your changes.  Even though you can use your nodes on any map, you can only save the changes you make to them while on HUB maps.

HUBs are special maps designed to hold many different nodes, each created by different players.  Think of a hotel, how it has many identical rooms.  You decorate one room in the hotel, while your friends each decorate another room in the hotel.  Together, you turn the HUB into a unique hangout for you and your friends.  You can host these HUBs multiplayer, or enjoy your friends' work in singleplayer mode thanks to the Steam workshop.

Walls & hotels are just the beginning.  Imagine convention halls or entire neighborhoods.  The stars are the limit.
